explanation: A prophet who preached a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, and who was the last great prophet before Jesus' public ministry began.
A deep inner change of heart where one turns away from sin and back to God, often accompanied by humility and a change in lifestyle.
A ritual act with water that symbolizes cleansing from sin and a public confession of turning to God's way.
An expression used to describe the Pharaonic descendants of Abraham, but also a metaphorical image that one can be reborn through faith rather than by bloodline alone.
A title meaning "the one who baptizes," referring to John's role in preparing the way for the Messiah by immersing people in water.
The divine Savior, also called Christ, whom God promised to send to save His people from their sins.
In contrast to John's water baptism, this refers to the inner cleansing and empowerment that Jesus will give through the Holy Spirit.
An action where one removes what is unnecessary or harmful to clear the way; here used of God's judgment on sin and the necessity of genuine repentance.
A picture that those who do not bear good fruit (genuine faith) will be cut down, while those who do will remain in God's kingdom.
